why:
MERGED 2026-09-07 during the phase-428 W10 rebase onto main, from two independent rows that both landed -- main's and this branch's. JSON keeps the LAST key, so one author's reasoning was being discarded silently. Both reached the same verdict; the prose is combined here and neither is lost.

`constexpr LifecycleTransition shutdown_transition_for(LifecycleState)` -- a free function in `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp`, added by issue 1099 (PR #602). REP-2002 gives shutdown THREE transition ids, one per legal source state (`5` from Unconfigured, `6` from Inactive, `7` from Active), so `LifecycleNode::shutdown()` cannot send a fixed id -- it used to send `5` unconditionally and so could not shut down an Inactive or Active node, which are the two states a node that has done any work is in. This function is that state->id mapping, the one place it is written; `shutdown()` is `trigger_transition(shutdown_transition_for(get_current_state()))`. The no-legal-shutdown states (`Unknown`, `Finalized`, `ErrorProcessing`) map to `ShutdownUnconfigured` ON PURPOSE, so the refusal comes from the state machine that owns the rule rather than a second copy of it here. rclcpp has no counterpart because it needs none: `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode::shutdown()` asks the rcl state machine, which resolves the label `"shutdown"` against the current state internally. Ours is a free `constexpr` rather than a member so a test can pin every arm without building an executor (`nros-cpp/tests/compile/lifecycle_transition_ids.cpp`). The same resolution lives in Rust as `nros_node::lifecycle`'s `shutdown()` and in the `ChangeState` service's handling of the generic `"shutdown"` label, so the C++ API, the Rust API and `ros2 lifecycle set <node> shutdown` agree about the same node.

`constexpr LifecycleTransition shutdown_transition_for(LifecycleState)` (`rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp:105`) -- the shutdown transition legal from a given state. REP-2002 gives shutdown THREE ids, one per legal source state, so no fixed id shuts a node down from an arbitrary state. rclcpp exposes no such helper: `LifecycleNode::shutdown()` resolves it inside `rcl_lifecycle`'s state machine, so the mapping is never a name a user writes.

Ours is public and `constexpr` for two reasons the issue that created it records. It is what `LifecycleNode::shutdown()` calls, after issue 1099 found it sending `5` unconditionally and therefore unable to shut down an Inactive or Active node; and being `constexpr` lets a test pin every arm without building an executor. The no-legal-shutdown states (`Unknown`, `Finalized`, `ErrorProcessing`) fall back to `ShutdownUnconfigured` on purpose, so the refusal comes from the state machine that owns the rule instead of being re-derived here. The Rust counterpart is `LifecycleTransition::from_shorthand(state, name)` (`nros-core/src/lifecycle.rs:122`), which does the same source-state-dependent resolution for the generic `"shutdown"` label a `ChangeState` request carries.
